settings.title: Access protection
settings.intro: nginx checks these rules before the site sees a request, for every file and page. Let's Encrypt still reaches the site, so certificates keep renewing. Behind a CDN such as Cloudflare, switch on the real visitor address under Operations first, or the rules see the CDN instead of the visitor.
settings.addressesHint: Addresses or ranges such as 203.0.113.0/24, one per line, at most {{max}}. Others get 403 Forbidden.
settings.yourAddress: Your address as the panel sees it: {{address}}
settings.lockout: Your own address is not on the list. You will not be able to open the site from here after saving.
settings.askPassword: Ask for a user name and password
settings.pathsHint: One per line, at most {{max}}. A path covers everything below it, in any upper or lower case: /wp-admin covers /wp-admin/ and /WP-Admin/users.php, not /wp-administrator.
settings.bypassHint: Optional, for example your office or an uptime monitor, one per line, at most {{max}}.
settings.passwordNote: The site's application no longer gets the browser's Authorization header on protected paths. Each protected request costs nginx a few milliseconds; on a busy site, protect only the admin paths. After 10 wrong passwords in 10 minutes, fail2ban blocks the address for an hour.

summary.paths_one: a password is asked on 1 path
summary.paths_other: a password is asked on {{count}} paths
summary.site: a password is asked for the whole site
